title: Tissue cell walls meet three at a time at 120°, regardless of cell size

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Tissue cell walls meet three at a time at 120°, regardless of cell size

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In sections of tissues such as plant parenchyma, as in a froth of soap-bubbles, cell walls meet three at a time at angles of 120° whatever the sizes of the cells, while the relative sizes of neighbouring cells determine only the curvature of the walls.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: walls meet three at a time at 120^\circ, independent of cell size; relative sizes set only wall curvature

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: in both cases we see the cell-walls everywhere meeting, by threes, at angles of 120°, irrespective of the size of the individual cells: whose relative size, on the other hand, determines the _curvature_ of the partition-walls.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates”; topic “Three-way junctions in tissues”. Scope: plant parenchyma, honeycomb, segmenting eggs and other cellular complexes viewed perpendicular to the walls

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: walls meet three at a time at 120^\circ, independent of cell size; relative sizes set only wall curvature

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch07-04: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.89

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Every element of the law maps directly to standard image-derived variables. Large open image collections and routine segmentation make a decisive test feasible, including quantification of exceptions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Segment planar tissue sections, measure junction valence, angles, cell areas, and wall curvature, and test whether triple junctions remain at 120 degrees independent of cell size.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Projection and section orientation can bias measured angles.

Rigid or actively stressed tissues may not satisfy equilibrium assumptions.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.9
data existence: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.9
operationalizability: 0.98
data adequacy: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Triple-junction angle and wall curvature are standard measurements on segmentations that can already be downloaded. The prediction that angle is independent of cell size while curvature is not is distinguishable from right-angle or random-junction alternatives. A small team can run that test on meristems, embryos and public epithelia with existing tools.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In three-dimensional segmentations of parenchyma, epithelia and early embryos, measure the angles at which walls meet and the curvature of walls between cells of different sizes. Triple junctions near 120 degrees regardless of cell size, with curvature set by the size difference, would support the claim; common four-way junctions, angles far from 120 degrees, or curvature unrelated to neighbouring sizes would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Honeycomb and every plant parenchyma type are not in these three collections.

Anisotropic stress and recent divisions are known to pull some junctions off 120 degrees, so the test needs a pre-registered exclusion or a report of that bias.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.8
data existence: 0.8
data adequacy: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.95
analysis feasibility: 0.85

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: If tissue cell walls meet three at a time at 120 degrees regardless of cell size, junction angles in real tissues cluster near 120 degrees more tightly than in a random partition of the plane, T-shaped junctions are rare, four cells do not meet at one point, and angle deviation does not depend on cell size.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: Cells in each image were segmented with Cellpose CPSAM v2 on the Nebius Scientific AI Platform (claim-sources/cell-geometry/segment.py; operation IDs and model checksum in claim-sources/cell-geometry/results/<image>/cellpose.json). claim-sources/cell-geometry/analyze.py closes inter-cell gaps, finds points where three or more cells meet, estimates each wall's direction from wall pixels 0.08-0.25 median cell diameters from the junction, counts neighbours of cells fully surrounded by segmented cells, and runs the same measurement on three synthetic tilings (hexagonal lattice, brick wall, random Voronoi) as calibration.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Exploratory, not pre-registered: the images were segmented and inspected before the pass criterion was written. Treat the verdict as hypothesis-generating; a pre-registered replication on new images is needed before it counts as a test. A tissue conforms if its junction-angle SD and its fraction of T-like junctions (largest angle >= 160 deg) are both below the random-Voronoi control. Supports if every usable tissue conforms; mixed if some do and some do not; refutes if none do.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Refutes if no tissue has both an angle SD and a T-junction fraction below the random-Voronoi control.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: tissues (of those usable) whose junction-angle SD and T-junction fraction are both below the random-Voronoi control, as measured on Cellpose-SAM output (see revisions for segmenter bias)

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Thompson's 'tissue cell walls' are taken as segmented cell outlines in 2D images of epithelia and epidermes; the angle is the angle between wall directions near the junction. The compound eye is included as a packing of ommatidia, not of single cells.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
Morphology of human corneal endothelium in situ.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

Drosophila eye 1000x - SEM MUSE.tif (Wikimedia Commons)

Physcomitrella patens (a, 144649-481016) 6961.JPG (Wikimedia Commons)

Epidermis of Festuca arundinacea.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

Aloe vera Cells, 150X.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Segmenter bias (added 2026-10-31 after external review): Cellpose-SAM pulls non-hexagonal packings toward 120-degree junctions (brick wall 100% -> 3-16% T-junctions). Conforming tissues are consistent with 120-degree packing but their margin over the random control is inflated; see revisions[0].

Exploratory, not pre-registered: the images were segmented and inspected before the pass criterion was written. Treat the verdict as hypothesis-generating; a pre-registered replication on new images is needed before it counts as a test.

One image per tissue, all from Wikimedia Commons; tissues were chosen by availability, not sampled.

Four-way junction fractions are upper bounds: the random-Voronoi control, which has no true four-way vertices, scores 8.6% because close three-way junctions merge.

Weak negative size-deviation correlations in some tissues also appear in the random control, so they are attributed to measurement noise in small cells.

The Drosophila eye image is an SEM of a curved surface; projection distorts its angles.
